review_method.normative_instructions: CLAUDE.md read fully; README.md read fully; SCHEMA.md and WORKFLOW.md consulted for repository and rendering-audit context.

review_method.source_snapshot_html: Reviewed each assigned frozen title and complete ItemBody; current source and frozen snapshot bytes and assigned HTML hashes were checked against the assignment.
review_method.tile_verification: Each screenshot hash was recomputed and matched its capture receipt. Every original tile was reviewed standalone with adjacent item context considered for crop boundaries, clipping, and label overlap.
review_method.boundary: No HTTP(S), live site, or network access; no production source/app/library/native/status edits, builds, tests, gates, commits, or pushes. Only lane-09.md and lane-09.json were written.

findings.claim: The explicitly described five-state SSP diagram is authored as raw centered TikZ rather than a renderer-recognized TikZ block. In the assigned ItemBody it appears as literal TeX commands instead of a graph, so the diagram is absent.
findings.intended_map: Vertices s,x,y,z,g; edges s→x (action a,c=1,p=1), s→y (action b,c=1,p=1), x→x (c=1,p=1/2), x→g (c=1,p=1/2), y→z (c=1,p=1), z→g (c=1,p=1), g→g (c=0,p=1).
findings.note: The literal-command appearance is present in both the standalone captured body and local assigned HTML; the tile split is at the capture boundary and does not create the appearance.

findings.claim: The rendered state/action graph has colliding labels around the two action branches: the “choose a/b” state-to-action labels and the reverse-transition probability labels occupy overlapping space near the center. This makes the four edge labels difficult to associate with their arrows.
findings.intended_map: One state s offers actions a and b; each action deterministically returns to s with reward 0 and probability 1. The graph semantics match the example; the issue is label placement.
findings.note: Confirmed on the standalone original-resolution tile in the diagram’s surrounding Remarks context. This is not a crop-edge or downscaling artifact.

diagram_candidates.proposal: A schematic belief-simplex view could show the upper envelope of finitely many alpha-vector linear forms, the maximizing regions R_alpha cut out by pairwise half-spaces, and a witness belief for a retained vector. A separate small policy-tree sketch could connect the exhaustive action/observation continuation rule to the candidate alpha-vector set and indicate why candidate count can grow exponentially.
diagram_candidates.concrete_relations: For each alpha, R_alpha consists of beliefs b with b·alpha≥b·beta for every beta; these regions cover Δ(S), and the value equals b·alpha on R_alpha. Witness pruning removes only vectors with no maximizing belief. For the count, P_{h+1}=A×P_h^Ω and N_{h+1}=|A|N_h^{|Ω|}.
diagram_candidates.caveat: Use an explicitly schematic, nonnumeric picture unless actual alpha vectors and a finite POMDP instance are supplied; do not imply polynomial pruning or an infinite-horizon representation. The proof does not rely on a figure.
